question: Where do the dead wait before the resurrection? Do Christians go to heaven at death?

answers.label: Souls wait in a hidden place until the resurrection
The faithful go at once to be with Christ in paradise

overview.text: Second-century writers stressed the resurrection: Justin calls those who say souls go to heaven at death, with no resurrection, no Christians at all, and Irenaeus has souls wait in the place appointed by God until the resurrection. Tertullian has souls wait in the underworld, with only martyrs in paradise.

By the third century Cyprian could speak of death as going home to paradise, where loved ones wait. In 1336 Benedict XII defined that the purified dead see God’s essence at once, before the resurrection; later teaching joined the two: the righteous are with Christ now and await the body’s resurrection.

quotes.author: Justin Martyr
quotes.english: If you meet some who are called Christians but do not confess this, but dare to blaspheme the God of Abraham, Isaac and Jacob, who say there is no resurrection of the dead, but that their souls are taken up into heaven at the moment of death, do not suppose they are Christians.
quotes.original: Εἰ γὰρ καὶ συνεβάλετε ὑμεῖς τισι λεγομένοις Χριστιανοῖς. καὶ τοῦτο μὴ ὁμολογοῦσιν, ἀλλὰ καὶ βλασφημεῖν τολμῶσι τὸν θεὸν Ἀβραὰμ καὶ τὸν θεὸν Ἰσαὰκ καὶ τὸν θεὸν Ἰακώβ. οἳ καὶ λέγουσι μὴ εἶναι νεκρῶν ἀνάστασιν, ἀλλὰ ἅμα τῷ ἀποθνήσκειν τὰς ψυχὰς αὐτῶν ἀναλαμβάνεσθαι εἰς τὸν οὐρανόν
quotes.context: Justin is attacking Gnostics who replaced the resurrection with the soul's flight to heaven, not every hope of being with Christ.

quotes.author: Irenaeus of Lyons
quotes.english: The souls go to the place appointed for them by God, and there they dwell until the resurrection, waiting for the resurrection; then, receiving their bodies back and rising whole, that is, bodily, just as the Lord also rose, they shall in this way come into the sight of God.
quotes.original: Αἱ ψυχαὶ ἀπέρχονται εἰς τὸν τόπον τὸν ὡρισμένον αὐταῖς ἀπὸ τοῦ Θεοῦ κἀκεῖ μέχρι τῆς ἀναστάσεως φοιτῶσι περιμένουσαι τὴν ἀνάστασιν· ἔπειτα ἀπολαβοῦσαι τὰ σώματα καὶ ὁλοκλήρως ἀναστᾶσαι, τουτέστι σωματικῶς, καθὼς καὶ ὁ Κύριος ἀνέστη, οὕτως ἐλεύσονται εἰς τὴν ὄψιν τοῦ Θεοῦ.
quotes.context: Irenaeus is opposing Gnostics who sent the saved soul straight up at death. Just before, he argues the Lord himself went to the place of the dead and rose bodily first; his disciples follow the same order. The passage survives in this Greek fragment and in the old Latin translation.

source.edition: Greek fragment, Migne PG 7 (Massuet), Khazarzar text

quotes.author: Tertullian
quotes.english: "But no," you say, "in paradise, to which the patriarchs and prophets have already moved from the underworld, as an appendage of the Lord's resurrection." Then how is it that the region of paradise, shown to John in the Spirit beneath the altar, shows no other souls in it but the martyrs? How did Perpetua, bravest martyr, on the day of her passion see only her fellow martyrs there, in her vision of paradise, unless the sword that guards paradise gives way to none but those who have died in Christ, not in Adam? ... Your own blood is the whole key to paradise.
quotes.original: immo, inquis, in paradiso, quo iam tunc et patriarchae et prophetae appendices dominicae resurrectionis ab inferis migrauerint. et quomodo Iohanni in spiritu paradisi regio reuelata, quae subicitur altari, nullas alias animas apud se praeter martyrum ostendit? quomodo Perpetua fortissima martyr sub die passionis in reuelatione paradisi solos illic commartyres suos uidit, nisi quia nullis romphaea paradisi ianitrix cedit nisi qui in Christo decesserint, non in Adam? ... tota paradisi clauis tuus sanguis est.
quotes.context: For Tertullian, souls wait in the underworld until the resurrection; only martyrs go at once to paradise.

quotes.author: Cyprian of Carthage
quotes.english: Let us welcome the day which assigns each of us to his own home, which snatches us from here, frees us from the snares of the world, and restores us to paradise and the kingdom. ... We count paradise as our homeland. ... A great number of our dear ones awaits us there: parents, brothers, children, a large and crowded throng longs for us, already sure of their own safety, still anxious for ours.
quotes.original: amplectamur diem qui adsignat singulos domicilio suo, qui nos istinc ereptos et laqueis saecularibus exsolutos paradiso restituit et regno. ... patriam nos nostram paradisum conputamus ... magnus illic nos carorum numerus expectat, parentum, fratrum, filiorum frequens nos et copiosa turba desiderat iam de sua incolumitate secura, adhuc de nostra salute sollicita.
quotes.context: Written during the plague of 252 to comfort Christians who feared dying in bed rather than as martyrs.

quotes.author: Pope Benedict XII
quotes.english: Immediately after their death, and after the purification already mentioned in those who needed such purification, even before they take up their bodies again and before the general judgment ... they were, are and will be in heaven, in the kingdom of heaven and in the heavenly paradise, with Christ, gathered into the company of the holy angels ... they saw and see the divine essence by a vision that is intuitive and also face to face, no creature coming between in the role of the object seen, but the divine essence showing itself to them directly, nakedly, clearly and openly ... the souls of those who have already died are truly blessed, and have life and eternal rest.
quotes.original: mox post mortem suam et purgationem praefatam in illis, qui purgatione huiusmodi indigebant, etiam ante resumptionem suorum corporum et iudicium generale ... fuerunt, sunt et erunt in coelo, coelorum regno et paradiso coelesti cum Christo, sanctorum Angelorum consortio aggregatae ... viderunt et vident divinam essentiam visione intuitiva et etiam faciali, nulla mediante creatura in ratione obiecti visi se habente, sed divina essentia immediate se nude, clare et aperte eis ostendente ... eorum animae, qui iam decesserunt, sunt vere beatae et habent vitam et requiem aeternam
quotes.context: The bull settled the dispute stirred by Pope John XXII, who had preached that the dead wait until the judgment to see God. Benedict defines the opposite for the purified: the sight of God at once, before the resurrection, while the body is still awaited. The scan of Denzinger is poorly OCRd, so the Latin follows the standard printed text.

quotes.author: Martin Luther
quotes.english: This, then, is the first place in all holy Scripture which testifies that the death of the saints is calm and precious in the sight of God: they do not taste death, but fall asleep most sweetly. ... The resting-places of souls are the word of God, that is, his promises, in which we fall asleep. ... we depart safe and quiet into the bosom of Christ.
quotes.original: Hic igitur primus locus est in tota scriptura sancta, qui testatur sanctorum mortem esse placidam et preciosam in conspectu Dei: non gustare eos mortem, sed suavissime obdormire. ... receptacula animarum sunt verbum Dei sive promissiones, in quibus obdormimus ... nos securos et quietos emigrare in sinum Christi
quotes.context: Luther on the death of Abraham, in the Genesis lectures printed in the Weimar Ausgabe: his fullest statement of the sleep of the dead. The search gap named his 1532 sermons, which are in German; this is the matching statement in the same Weimar edition, in Latin. The sleep is a rest held in God's word and promise until the resurrection.

source.edition: D. Martin Luthers Werke, kritische Gesamtausgabe (Weimar Ausgabe), vol. 43

quotes.author: Westminster Assembly
quotes.english: Besides these two places, for souls separated from their bodies, the Scripture acknowledgeth none.
quotes.original: Besides these two places, for souls separated from their bodies, the Scripture acknowledgeth none.
quotes.context: The full section says the souls of the righteous are "received into the highest heavens" to wait for the redemption of their bodies.

method: Every early quote was read in its Greek or Latin and translated for this page by Claude (Opus 5.5) on 13 October 2026. Each line names the printed edition it was read from.
